Remark.content: Original flush-mount vault found crushed and the PVC casing stub deteriorated during routine site inspection. Protective monument and casing stub replaced; new top-of-casing reference notch established 6 in (0.1524 m) higher than the original as-built reference point. Existing casing/screen depth values (measured from top of casing) remain valid unchanged since the centerline reference was shifted uniformly.

Equipment.gml:name: Pitcher Barrel Sampler, 3-in Shelby Tube Liner

Specification.gml:name: Pitcher Sampler

Remark.content: Undisturbed samples obtained using a Pitcher-type rotary core barrel fitted with a stationary 3-in OD, 0.083-in wall thin-wall (Shelby) tube sampler. The tube is advanced ahead of the rotating, fluid-flushed outer barrel, minimizing disturbance to the recovered soil in variably stiff or interbedded materials where a directly pushed thin-wall tube would refuse, per ASTM D1587/D1587M-15.

Specification.standardTitle: Standard Practice for Thin-Walled Tube Sampling of Fine-Grained Soils for Geotechnical Purposes

Parameter.parameterValue: Crew 2 - J. Alvarez (driller), M. Reyes (field geologist)

ParticleSizeTest.gml:description: Hydrometer particle size analysis performed on Sample ST-4 (80.0-82.5 ft), lean CLAY with sand (CL), within the 61-85 ft interval, roughly midway between the nearby Atterberg results at 65 ft (Test_ATT_BH-Mockup-1_65, LL=31, PI=13) and 85 ft (Test_ATT_BH-Mockup-1_85, LL=58, PI=34) at the top of the underlying CH unit. Specimen was assessed in the field and by the laboratory technician as essentially 100 percent fine-grained by texture; dry sieve analysis was not performed, per laboratory discretion, and the full specimen mass was processed directly by hydrometer.

PorePressureDissipationTest.gml:description: Pore pressure dissipation test performed at 28.0 ft (along-hole) in a stiff sandy silt/silty sand unit encountered above the 40 ft transition into finer material. The u2 reading at the start of the hold matched the CPTu profile's own continuously-logged u2 at this depth and was already close to the estimated hydrostatic equilibrium, rising only marginally over the hold and confirming free-draining conditions with negligible excess pore pressure generated during penetration; back-calculation of ch/kh was not attempted given the negligible, poorly-defined dissipation signal typical of this material.
PorePressureDissipationTest.gml:name: Sounding-Mockup-1 PPDT-1

Remark.content: Cone advancement halted at 28.0 ft and held stationary for 300 s while u2 was logged; the reading (0.295 tonf/ft2 at the start of the hold, matching the CPTu profile's own continuously-logged u2 at this depth) rose only marginally to 0.312 tonf/ft2, consistent with a free-draining silty sand/sandy silt already near hydrostatic equilibrium rather than a plastic fine-grained soil generating significant excess pore pressure.

Specification.gml:name: Pore-Water Pressure Dissipation Test — ASTM D5778 Annex A2
Specification.standardTitle: Standard Test Method for Electronic Friction Cone and Piezocone Penetration Testing of Soils — Annex A2, Pore-Water Pressure Dissipation Test

PorePressureDissipationTest.gml:description: Pore pressure dissipation test performed at 65.0 ft (along-hole) in a soft, normally consolidated clay unit corresponding to the low-tip-resistance, high-excess-pore-pressure zone identified on the CPTu profile between roughly 50 and 90 ft. Dissipation was slow and did not fully reach equilibrium within the 3600 s monitoring period; U50 was well defined and used with an assumed rigidity index to back-calculate ch.
PorePressureDissipationTest.gml:name: Sounding-Mockup-1 PPDT-2

Remark.content: Test extended to 3600 s (60 min) per field protocol for suspected soft clay; u2 was still decreasing slowly at test termination (1.507 tonf/ft2 vs. an estimated hydrostatic U0 of 1.468 tonf/ft2) and had not reached full equilibrium. T50 was picked directly off the recorded curve at approximately 660 s.

Specification.gml:name: Pore-Water Pressure Dissipation Test — ASTM D5778 Annex A2
Specification.standardTitle: Standard Test Method for Electronic Friction Cone and Piezocone Penetration Testing of Soils — Annex A2, Pore-Water Pressure Dissipation Test

StaticConePenetrationTest.gml:name: CPT-2 Piezocone Push Log

Remark.content: Piezocone push advanced adjacent to the BH-Mockup-3 collar to extend the electronic CPTu profile beneath the paved section.

StaticConePenetrationTest.frictionReducer: Friction reducer sleeve installed 1 m behind the cone tip to reduce rod friction through the dense gravel units above 20 ft
StaticConePenetrationTest.pushRodType: A-rod, 36 mm OD threaded push rod

Remark.content: Push halted at 45.0 ft in a fine-grained unit below the dense near-surface gravel; u2 at the start of the hold (0.663 tonf/ft2, matching the CPTu profile's own continuously-logged u2 at this depth) was already close to the estimated hydrostatic equilibrium and rose only modestly over the 900 s hold to 0.780 tonf/ft2 (T50 picked at roughly 120 s off the recorded curve), indicating limited excess pore pressure was generated during penetration at this depth.

Monitor.gml:name: MW-1 Water Level and Temperature Monitoring

Remark.content: Water levels and temperature recorded once daily by an in-well pressure transducer beginning 2025-06-04, the day following MW-1 completion, continuing to present. MW-1 is completed in the shallow, unconfined water-table aquifer (screened 36-46 ft below top of casing); levels fluctuate gradually and seasonally, rising through winter recharge and falling through summer.

Monitor.gml:name: MW-2 Water Level and Temperature Monitoring

Remark.content: Water levels and temperature recorded once daily by an in-well pressure transducer beginning 2025-06-04, the day following MW-2 completion, continuing to present. MW-2 is completed in a deeper confined sand aquifer (screened 106-126 ft below top of casing); the potentiometric surface sits well above the screen and shows larger, more erratic fluctuations than MW-1, reflecting the influence of a nearby production well operating on a weekday pumping schedule (drawdown accumulating Monday-Friday, recovering over the weekend), superimposed on a muted seasonal trend. On 2026-04-06 the protective monument and casing stub were repaired and the top-of-casing reference point was reset 0.5 ft (0.1524 m) higher than the original as-built elevation (see samplingFeatureRef Well/maintenanceEvent). This reference point change causes a corresponding ~0.5 ft step increase in reported depth-to-water at that date with no discontinuity in reported water elevation, which is computed relative to each reading's own then-current reference point.

PointLocation.gml:description: Original as-built top of casing, flush-mount vault, prior to the 2026-04-06 protective monument repair and reference point reset (see maintenanceEvent).
